text: The chapter describes HDF5 as a better choice than Zarr for parallel, cloud-native access to large chunked-array datasets such as those used in AnnData.
explanation: This is reversed. The chapter presents Zarr as the cloud-friendly, chunked-array format that is better than HDF5 for parallel access from cloud object storage (S3, GCS), which is why AnnData can use a Zarr backing. HDF5/h5py remains useful for local structured storage of simulation trajectories, but it is not presented as the superior choice for parallel, cloud-native access.
